claims.statement: The Boundary meta-workspace declares six VCS-connected staging L3 workspaces in the rosa-boundary project: credentials, account, two networks and two regional runtimes, all pinned to Terraform 1.16.0. Each network pair and runtime pair reuses a source working directory while retaining separate workspace state.

The staging AWS-credentials stack's default role group allowlists all six Boundary workspaces, including the west network and regional workspaces, and the Boundary meta-workspace binds its generated default AWS dynamic credentials variable set to each of them.
The AWS-credentials workspace binds a project-scoped TFE-token set alongside its generated AWS dynamic credentials set; the network, account and regional workspaces bind only the generated AWS set.

All six staging L3 workspaces now set auto_apply = true and auto_apply_run_trigger = true, either explicitly (rosa-boundary-stage-network-us-west-2, rosa-boundary-stage-account, rosa-boundary-stage-regional, rosa-boundary-stage-regional-us-west-2) or by inheriting the called module's default (rosa-boundary-stage-network, rosa-boundary-stage-aws-creds), so every ordinary staging apply proceeds without manual confirmation. The explicit manual-apply gate (auto_apply = false, auto_apply_run_trigger = false, execution_mode = "remote") has moved to the two new production workspaces, rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds and rosa-boundary-prod-account.

Both regional workspaces receive their own VPC and private-subnet IDs as explicit Git-managed L2 variables; the current map does not transfer network outputs through remote state or declare network-to-regional source-workspace run triggers.

The Boundary meta-workspace calls version 0.0.23 (not 0.0.15) of the private TFE workspaces module to declare notifications, Git-managed variables and variable-set bindings; this single module call now declares eight L3 workspaces -- six staging workspaces in the rosa-boundary-stage AWS account plus two bootstrapping production workspaces (rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds, rosa-boundary-prod-account) in the separate rosa-boundary-prod AWS account.

The AWS-credentials provider is guarded to staging account 150100906299 and its TFE provider targets hp-platform-engineering; its default role group allowlists six Boundary project workspaces, while Trusted Actions is configured in a separate role group. Network and regional providers independently enforce allowed_account_ids guards.

A single account L3 workspace owns shared IAM identities, common managed-policy attachments including investigation-reaper VPC execution, user OIDC providers, the Bedrock budget and model agreements, independently of regional resource states.

The separate rosa-trusted-actions credentials role group allowlists global and stage workspaces and adds a secret-pattern-scoped secretsmanager:GetSecretValue policy to its plan role alongside ReadOnlyAccess, without adding that permission to Boundary's default plan group or overriding the apply-role policy defaults.

Both staging regional workspaces use the same rosa-boundary-stage role prefix and us-east-1 legacy_policy_region; the regional naming rule keeps east inline-policy names unsuffixed and appends -us-west-2 in west, so distinct regional grants accumulate on shared account roles rather than isolating their permissions.

Staging's account input explicitly approves us-east-1 and us-west-2 for the shared Bedrock logging role; the role retains SourceAccount restriction and permits only the configured regional SourceArn patterns, while invocation-log destinations and delivery grants remain regional.

The meta-workspace's L2 map defines a second, separate AWS account bootstrap: rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds and rosa-boundary-prod-account target AWS account 514903006123, distinct from the staging account 150100906299, via their own provider guard, cloud.tf workspace name, and generated dynamic-credentials module instance.

The production credentials stack's default role group allowlists only rosa-boundary-prod-aws-creds and rosa-boundary-prod-account, with a comment that workload workspaces are authorized separately after registration; there is no production network or regional workspace yet, so the production account currently has no VPC, ECS, or Lambda runtime.

rosa-boundary-prod-account reuses the deploy/account working directory with production-specific Git-managed variables: role_name_prefix = "rosa-boundary-prod", stage = "prod", aws_account_id = "514903006123", legacy_policy_region/legacy_role_tag_region both "us-east-1", bedrock_logging_source_regions pre-authorizing ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"] for both planned production regions, and adopt_existing_resources = false reflecting a greenfield account.
